local_seasons.the plum rains and summer flood season: the plum rains and summer flood season

flood-docs.text: Put ID cards, land papers and phone numbers in a sealed plastic bag.
flood-docs.why: Papers are the hardest thing to replace after a flood.

flood-route.text: Agree with your household on a high place to go and a way to get there.
flood-route.why: Deciding in the dark, in the rain, is when people get hurt.

flood-water.text: Store clean drinking water in closed containers, enough for three days.
flood-water.why: Floods pollute wells and taps first.

flood-drains.text: Clear drains, gutters and channels near your home now.
flood-drains.why: Blocked drains turn heavy rain into a flood in your yard.

flood-raise.text: Move food, seeds, fertiliser and valuables off the floor.
flood-raise.why: Even shallow water ruins stored food and seed.

flood-animals.text: Plan where animals can go on higher ground.
flood-animals.why: Livestock losses are often the biggest cost of a flood.

flood-warnings.text: Find out how your local warnings are given: radio, SMS, loudspeaker or a neighbour.
flood-warnings.why: The official warning is the signal to act.

flood-medical.text: Keep a week of any daily medicines in the emergency bag.
flood-medical.why: Clinics may be cut off for days.

river-level.text: Learn where the river reached in the last big flood and stay above that line.
river-level.why: Past high-water marks are the best local guide.

flash-avoid.text: Never cross a flooded road or dry riverbed during heavy rain.
flash-avoid.why: Most flash-flood deaths happen in vehicles and river crossings.

slide-signs.text: Watch for new cracks, tilting trees or springs on slopes above your home.
slide-signs.why: Slopes give warning signs before they fail.

slide-move.text: If you live below a steep slope, arrange a safer place to sleep during heavy rain.
slide-move.why: Landslides mostly strike at night after days of rain.

drought-store.text: Fix leaks and add water storage: tanks, drums, or a covered pit.
drought-store.why: Every litre saved now is a litre you do not have to carry later.

drought-seed.text: Ask your extension officer about early-maturing or drought-tolerant seed.
drought-seed.why: Short-season crops can finish before the rains stop.

drought-plant.text: Plant staggered: some early, some at normal time, not all at once.
drought-plant.why: Spreads the risk of a false start to the rains.

drought-fodder.text: Cut and store extra fodder; consider selling weak animals early.
drought-fodder.why: Prices fall once everyone sells at the same time.

drought-food.text: Buy staple food a little at a time now while prices are normal.
drought-food.why: Food prices rise fastest when harvests fail.

drought-share.text: Agree with neighbours how a shared well or tank will be rationed.
drought-share.why: Agreed rules prevent conflict when water gets short.

droughtne-store.text: Store water and plan irrigation if you are in the north or east.
droughtne-store.why: El Niño summers are often dry there.

water-reuse.text: Reuse washing water for gardens and toilets.
water-reuse.why: Cuts household water use by a third.

water-schedule.text: Learn your city's water rationing schedule and fill containers on supply days.
water-schedule.why: Cities ration during dry seasons; knowing the day avoids empty taps.

fire-clear.text: Clear dry grass and brush at least 10 metres around buildings.
fire-clear.why: A cleared strip stops most grass fires reaching a house.

fire-noburn.text: Do not burn fields or rubbish on hot, windy days.
fire-noburn.why: Most large fires start as a controlled burn that escaped.

bush-plan.text: Make a leave-early plan and follow your fire service's danger ratings.
bush-plan.why: Leaving late is the most dangerous choice in a bushfire.

wild-plan.text: Prepare an evacuation bag and know two ways out of your area.
wild-plan.why: Wildfires can close the main road within minutes.

haze-mask.text: Keep masks for smoke days and a room that can be closed off.
haze-mask.why: Smoke haze harms children and the elderly most.

heat-hours.text: Move hard work to early morning and late afternoon.
heat-hours.why: Heat illness peaks in the middle of the day.

heat-check.text: Check daily on elderly neighbours and people living alone.
heat-check.why: Most heat deaths happen quietly at home.

heat-water.text: Drink water often, before you feel thirsty.
heat-water.why: Thirst comes late when the body is already short of water.

disease-water.text: Boil or treat drinking water when floods reach wells or pipes.
disease-water.why: Cholera and diarrhoea spread through flood water.

disease-mosquito.text: Empty standing water around the home every few days and use nets.
disease-mosquito.why: Mosquito diseases rise after heavy rain.

cholera-ors.text: Keep oral rehydration salts at home and know the nearest clinic.
cholera-ors.why: Fast rehydration saves lives in cholera outbreaks.

rvf-animals.text: Report sudden animal deaths or abortions to a vet, and avoid handling sick animals.
rvf-animals.why: Rift Valley fever spreads to people from sick livestock after floods.

crop-mulch.text: Mulch fields to hold soil moisture.
crop-mulch.why: Mulch can keep soil moist for an extra week or two.

cropfail-diversify.text: Plant a mix of crops, including some that need less water.
cropfail-diversify.why: One failed crop hurts less when others survive.

cropfail-insurance.text: Ask about crop insurance or a farmer group support scheme before planting.
cropfail-insurance.why: Most schemes close their sign-up before the season starts.

food-network.text: Find out which local groups give food or cash support and how to register.
food-network.why: Registering early avoids queues when help arrives.

hurr-kit.text: Prepare a hurricane kit: water, food, torch, radio, medicines, documents.
hurr-kit.why: Shops and power may be out for days after a storm.

hurr-shelter.text: Know your nearest shelter and how you will get there.
hurr-shelter.why: Shelters fill fast once a warning is issued.

typh-kit.text: Prepare a typhoon kit: water, food, torch, radio, medicines, documents.
typh-kit.why: Shops and power may be out for days after a storm.

typh-boats.text: Fishers: agree a safe harbour plan and follow no-sail warnings.
typh-boats.why: Most typhoon deaths at sea are boats caught out.

cyc-kit.text: Prepare a cyclone kit: water, food, torch, radio, medicines, documents.
cyc-kit.why: Shops and power may be out for days after a storm.

cyc-roof.text: Tie down or repair loose roofing before the season.
cyc-roof.why: Loose roof sheets are the main cause of cyclone damage and injury.

cycmoz-plan.text: Know your evacuation route and shelter before the cyclone season.
cycmoz-plan.why: Cyclones in the Mozambique Channel bring floods far inland.

cycshift-plan.text: Prepare for cyclones even if your island is rarely hit.
cycshift-plan.why: During El Niño, cyclones form and travel farther east than usual.

storm-trees.text: Trim weak branches and secure loose items outdoors.
storm-trees.why: Falling branches cause most storm damage to homes.

seas-move.text: Move valuables and sleeping areas away from the shoreline during king tides.
seas-move.why: Sea level is higher than normal on Pacific atolls during El Niño.

salt-store.text: Store fresh water before the dry season; test wells for salt.
salt-store.why: Low river flow lets sea water push into wells and canals.

frost-cover.text: Cover seedlings at night and keep seed for replanting.
frost-cover.why: Highland frost during dry spells can kill a whole crop overnight.

snow-water.text: Expect lower rivers next summer; plan irrigation and water use early.
snow-water.why: Less winter snow means less water later in the year.

snow-kit.text: Keep extra food, heating fuel and medicines in case roads close.
snow-kit.why: Heavy snow can cut off towns for days.

cold-heat.text: Check heating, insulation and warm clothing before winter.
cold-heat.why: Cold snaps hit older people and babies hardest.

spring-melt.text: Expect higher rivers in spring when heavy snow melts.
spring-melt.why: A snowy winter often means spring floods.

mild-pests.text: Watch for more pests and mould; a mild winter kills fewer of them.
mild-pests.why: Cold normally keeps pests and disease in check.

cool-crop.text: Choose crop varieties that ripen in a cooler, wetter summer.
cool-crop.why: Cool summers delay ripening and increase crop disease.

always-official.text: Follow your national weather service for warnings; this briefing is a seasonal outlook, not a warning.
always-official.why: Only official services issue alerts for specific days and places.

always-share.text: Tell one neighbour what this season may bring.
always-share.why: Communities that talk about risk early prepare better.

peru-ecuador-coast.name: Coastal Peru and Ecuador
peru-ecuador-coast.el_nino_note: Warm coastal water brings heavy rain to a normally dry coast. 1982-83, 1997-98 and 2017 brought severe floods.

northern-south-america.name: Northern South America and the Amazon
northern-south-america.el_nino_note: Weaker rains and heat raise fire and river-low-water risk across the Orinoco and Amazon basins.
northern-south-america.la_nina_note: Heavier rains, especially in Colombia and Venezuela.

northeast-brazil.name: Northeast Brazil (Nordeste)
northeast-brazil.el_nino_note: The main rainy season often fails or comes late in strong El Niño years.
northeast-brazil.la_nina_note: Rainy season tends to be stronger.

southeast-south-america.name: Southeastern South America
southeast-south-america.el_nino_note: Southern Brazil, Uruguay, northeastern Argentina and Paraguay usually get heavy spring and summer rain and river floods.
southeast-south-america.la_nina_note: Drier spring and summer; crop stress is common.

central-chile.name: Central Chile
central-chile.el_nino_note: Winter storms tend to be wetter.
central-chile.la_nina_note: Winter rains tend to be weak.

altiplano.name: Andean highlands (Altiplano)
altiplano.el_nino_note: Summer rains tend to be weaker on the high plateau; the coast below can be wet at the same time.

central-america-dry-corridor.name: Central America and southern Mexico
central-america-dry-corridor.el_nino_note: Rainy season starts late and the mid-summer dry spell (canícula) is longer, especially in the Dry Corridor.
central-america-dry-corridor.la_nina_note: More rain and a more active Atlantic hurricane season.

caribbean.name: Caribbean islands
caribbean.el_nino_note: Drier wet season and usually fewer Atlantic hurricanes.

southern-us-north-mexico.name: Southern United States and northern Mexico
southern-us-north-mexico.el_nino_note: A stronger jet stream steers more winter storms across California, the Southwest, Texas, the Gulf coast and the Southeast.
southern-us-north-mexico.la_nina_note: Winter tends to be dry and warm across the southern states.

us-pacific-northwest.name: Pacific Northwest and western Canada
us-pacific-northwest.el_nino_note: Milder, drier winters and less mountain snow.
us-pacific-northwest.la_nina_note: Cooler, wetter winters with more snow.

northern-us-southern-canada.name: Northern United States and southern Canada
northern-us-southern-canada.el_nino_note: Winters tend to be milder than usual across the northern Plains, Midwest and Great Lakes.
northern-us-southern-canada.la_nina_note: Colder, snowier winters in the northern tier and Ohio Valley.

alaska.name: Alaska
alaska.el_nino_note: Winters are usually much warmer than normal.

hawaii.name: Hawaii
hawaii.el_nino_note: Wet season is often weak; drought risk rises in late winter and spring.

india-monsoon.name: India, Pakistan, Nepal and Bangladesh (summer monsoon)
india-monsoon.el_nino_note: The summer monsoon tends to be weaker and patchier. Not every El Niño brings drought, but the risk is clearly higher.
india-monsoon.la_nina_note: Monsoon tends to be stronger with more floods.

sri-lanka-south-india.name: Sri Lanka and southern India (northeast monsoon)
sri-lanka-south-india.el_nino_note: The October-December rains tend to be heavier.

maritime-continent.name: Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Brunei and Timor-Leste
maritime-continent.el_nino_note: The dry season is longer and harsher and the rainy season starts late. Forest and peat fires and smoke haze were severe in 1997 and 2015.
maritime-continent.la_nina_note: Wetter dry season and heavier rainy season.

philippines.name: Philippines
philippines.el_nino_note: Rain falls below normal from late in the year through the following dry season. Typhoons tend to form farther east and can be stronger.
philippines.la_nina_note: Wetter, with more typhoons crossing the islands.

mainland-southeast-asia.name: Vietnam, Thailand, Cambodia, Laos and Myanmar
mainland-southeast-asia.el_nino_note: Hotter, drier dry season; late monsoon onset; low Mekong flows and salt intrusion in the delta.

southern-china.name: Southern China and the Yangtze basin
southern-china.el_nino_note: Wetter winter and spring, and the summer after a strong El Niño often brings Yangtze flooding (1998, 2016).
southern-china.la_nina_note: Colder, drier winters; signal is variable.

northern-china-korea-japan.name: Northern China, Korea and Japan
northern-china-korea-japan.el_nino_note: Winters lean mild; summer signal is weak and mixed.

png-melanesia.name: Papua New Guinea, Solomon Islands and Vanuatu
png-melanesia.el_nino_note: Long dry spells; highland frost and crop loss in PNG in 1997 and 2015.
png-melanesia.la_nina_note: Wetter, with cyclones more likely to the west.

central-pacific-islands.name: Kiribati, Tuvalu, Nauru and the Marshall Islands
central-pacific-islands.el_nino_note: Rain moves toward the central Pacific; equatorial atolls become much wetter, with higher sea levels in some areas.

southwest-pacific-islands.name: Fiji, Tonga, Samoa, Cook Islands and New Caledonia
southwest-pacific-islands.el_nino_note: The main rain band shifts northeast, so Fiji, Tonga and New Caledonia tend to be drier. Cyclones can reach farther east than usual.

eastern-australia.name: Eastern and northern Australia
eastern-australia.el_nino_note: Winter and spring rain is usually well below normal, with more heatwaves and bushfire risk; the northern wet season starts later.
eastern-australia.la_nina_note: Wetter, with more floods and more tropical cyclones.

southwest-australia.name: Southwestern and southern Australia
southwest-australia.el_nino_note: Signal is weaker than in the east.

new-zealand.name: New Zealand
new-zealand.el_nino_note: Stronger westerly winds: drier in the northeast, wetter in the southwest, cooler overall.
new-zealand.la_nina_note: More northeasterly winds bring rain to the north and east.

east-africa-short-rains.name: Kenya, Somalia, southern Ethiopia, Uganda and northern Tanzania
east-africa-short-rains.el_nino_note: The October-December short rains are usually heavy, with flooding along rivers and in low areas. 1997 and 2023 saw severe floods.
east-africa-short-rains.la_nina_note: Short rains fail more often; repeated La Niña years led to the 2020-23 Horn of Africa drought.

ethiopia-sudan-summer.name: Ethiopian highlands, Eritrea and Sudan (summer rains)
ethiopia-sudan-summer.el_nino_note: The main kiremt rains tend to be weaker; 2015 brought a severe drought in Ethiopia.

southern-africa.name: Southern Africa
southern-africa.el_nino_note: Summer rains are usually below normal with hot spells; maize harvests failed widely in 1992, 2016 and 2024.

madagascar.name: Madagascar
madagascar.el_nino_note: The south and west tend to be drier; cyclone activity shifts.

sahel.name: The Sahel and northern Nigeria
sahel.el_nino_note: Tendency toward a weaker rainy season, but Atlantic and Indian Ocean temperatures matter more here.

gulf-of-guinea.name: West African coast (Gulf of Guinea)
gulf-of-guinea.el_nino_note: No reliable rainfall signal; slightly warmer.

central-africa.name: Central Africa (Congo basin)
central-africa.el_nino_note: Weak rainfall signal; warmer than normal is common.

southwest-asia.name: Iran, Iraq, Afghanistan, northern Pakistan and the Arabian Peninsula
southwest-asia.el_nino_note: Winter and spring rains tend to be heavier, sometimes causing flash floods in dry areas.
southwest-asia.la_nina_note: Winter rains and snow tend to be weak; drought risk rises.

north-africa-mediterranean.name: North Africa and the Mediterranean
north-africa-mediterranean.el_nino_note: ENSO has little consistent effect here. Local forecasts matter more.

europe.name: Europe
europe.el_nino_note: Any effect is weak and inconsistent. Use your national forecast.

canada-arctic.name: Northern Canada and Greenland
canada-arctic.el_nino_note: Western and central Canada usually have milder winters.

southeast-brazil.name: Southeastern Brazil (São Paulo, Rio, Minas Gerais)
southeast-brazil.el_nino_note: Sits between the wet south and the dry north; rain signal is mixed, heat is more likely.

mexico-north-us-southwest.name: US Southwest and northwestern Mexico
mexico-north-us-southwest.el_nino_note: Wetter winters across Arizona, New Mexico, Texas and northern Mexico.
mexico-north-us-southwest.la_nina_note: Dry, warm winters; drought risk rises.

south-atlantic-uruguay.name: Uruguay and the Pampas
south-atlantic-uruguay.la_nina_note: Drought risk is high; 2022-23 was severe.

tanzania-south-mozambique-north.name: Southern Tanzania and northern Mozambique
tanzania-south-mozambique-north.el_nino_note: On the border between wetter East Africa and drier Southern Africa; local outlooks matter.

japan.name: Japan
japan.el_nino_note: Mild winters and cool, wet summers are somewhat more common.
japan.la_nina_note: Cold winters and hot summers are somewhat more common.
